data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Log-based protocols are provably safer than lease-based rivals because they enforce the causal latency invariant that seal-visibility latency is strictly bounded above by failure-detection latency, whereas lease-based protocols conflate death detection with displacement permission and therefore violate this invariant under partial synchrony.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The log implementation allows silent truncation or fork","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Reclamation reads a stale snapshot and misses a recent seal","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Log availability is worse than workspace host availability, causing indefinite stall","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Completed evidence is sealed into an append-only shared log before workspace release. Reclamation reads the log tail for the problem ID; if no seal is visible, reclamation must stall indefinitely. The durable record must contain: (1) the log sequence number, (2) the content-addressed evidence hash at that sequence, and (3) a signed checkpoint of the log prefix. Adjudication favors the log because it externalizes the happens-before relation: the log records completion before reclamation can observe death, whereas a lease merely infers death from timeout and cannot distinguish silent displacement from slow heartbeat.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
